label: Treaty of Troyes
why: Henry V becomes heir and regent of France, the Council of Constance has ended the Schism, the Hussite wars have begun, the Ottomans are reunited and Ming rules Dai Viet while moving its court to Beijing.

realms.name: Kingdom of England
realms.note: Holds Normandy (conquered 1417-19), Calais, Gascony and the Lordship of Ireland; named heir and regent of France at Troyes this day.

realms.name: Kingdom of France (Charles VI)
realms.ruler: Charles VI (mentally ill; government in Burgundian hands)
realms.note: The Paris/Troyes crown that signs Troyes, disinheriting the Dauphin. Paris held by the Burgundian party since May 1418.

realms.name: Dauphinist France (Kingdom of Bourges)
realms.ruler: Dauphin Charles (regent by his own claim since 1418)
realms.note: Loire, the Centre, Languedoc and Dauphiné; Armagnac party with Scottish allies.

realms.name: Valois Burgundy
realms.note: Duchy and County of Burgundy, Flanders, Artois; allied with England since the murder at Montereau (1419).

realms.name: Duchy of Brittany
realms.ruler: John V (held captive by the Penthièvre, Feb-Jul 1420; Duchess Joan rules)

realms.name: County of Provence (Angevin)
realms.ruler: Louis III of Anjou (with his mother Yolande of Aragon)

realms.name: Duchy of Bar
realms.ruler: Cardinal Louis of Bar (René of Anjou his heir, married to Isabella of Lorraine in Oct 1420)

realms.name: Kingdom of Scotland
realms.ruler: James I (captive in England); Robert, Duke of Albany, governor

realms.name: Kingdom of Portugal
realms.note: Holds Ceuta since 1415.

realms.name: Crown of Castile
realms.note: Court itinerant; Infantes of Aragon dominant around the young king.

realms.name: Crown of Aragon
realms.note: Trastámara since Caspe (1412); holds Sicily and Sardinia claims; Alfonso sails for Sardinia and Corsica in May 1420.

realms.name: Marinid Morocco
realms.ruler: Abu Said Uthman III (murdered in 1420; then the infant Abd al-Haqq II under Wattasid regency)

realms.name: Hafsid Sultanate
realms.note: Expanding west: Algiers and Constantine region under Hafsid rule.

realms.name: Duchy of Savoy
realms.note: Gains Piedmont (Achaea branch) in 1418.

realms.name: Duchy of Milan
realms.note: Rebuilding the Visconti state; buys Genoa in 1421.

realms.name: Republic of Venice
realms.note: Mainland state from 1404-05 (Vicenza, Verona, Padua); finishing the conquest of Friuli (Udine falls June 1420).

realms.name: Republic of Genoa
realms.note: Holds Caffa and Gazaria, Pera, Chios through the Maona.

realms.name: Republic of Florence
realms.note: Pope Martin V resides in Florence until Sept 1420.

realms.name: Patriarchate of Aquileia (Friuli)
realms.note: Being conquered by Venice; Udine surrenders 6 June 1420.

realms.name: Papal States
realms.ruler: Martin V (in Florence; enters Rome Sept 1420)
realms.note: Schism ended; much of the Patrimony held by condottieri (Braccio da Montone in Perugia).

realms.name: Kingdom of Naples
realms.note: Louis III of Anjou's claim revived; war from summer 1420, Joanna adopts Alfonso V in Sept.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hungary
realms.ruler: Sigismund (King of the Romans; claims Bohemia)
realms.note: Sigismund's power base; he is in Bohemia/Silesia leading the anti-Hussite crusade.

realms.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
realms.ruler: Contested: Sigismund claims (crowned 28 Jul 1420); Hussite estates and Prague towns reject him
realms.note: Interregnum since Wenceslaus IV died (Aug 1419); royal garrisons hold the Prague castles.

realms.name: Tábor (Hussite radicals)
realms.ruler: Hussite captains (Jan Žižka, Mikuláš of Hus)
realms.note: Founded Feb-Mar 1420.

realms.name: Duchy of Austria
realms.note: Albertine line; Sigismund's son-in-law to be (1421).

realms.name: County of Tyrol
realms.ruler: Frederick IV of the Empty Pockets

realms.name: Bavaria-Munich
realms.note: Bavaria split into Munich, Ingolstadt, Landshut and Straubing lines.

realms.name: Margraviate of Meissen (Wettin)
realms.note: Wettin lands, not yet electors (Saxe-Wittenberg passes to them in 1423).

realms.name: Margraviate of Brandenburg
realms.note: Enfeoffed at Constance in 1415.

realms.name: Free City of Lübeck
realms.note: Head of the Hanse.

realms.name: Electorate of Cologne
realms.note: The city of Cologne governs itself as a free city within the electorate.

realms.name: Holland and Zeeland
realms.ruler: John of Bavaria (governing; Jacqueline of Hainaut's rights pledged to him April 1420)

realms.name: Duchy of Brabant
realms.note: Burgundian cadet line.

realms.name: Teutonic Order (Prussia)
realms.ruler: Grand Master Michael Küchmeister von Sternberg
realms.note: Weakened after Grunwald (1410) and the Hunger War (1414).

realms.name: Livonian Order
realms.note: Dominates the city of Riga.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
realms.note: Under the Polish crown's union (Horodło 1413) but ruled independently; holds Kyiv and Smolensk.

realms.name: Denmark (Kalmar Union)
realms.note: Union king of Denmark, Norway and Sweden; at war with Holstein over Schleswig; holds Gotland since 1408.

realms.name: Sweden (Kalmar Union)
realms.note: Personal union under Eric.

realms.name: Norway (Kalmar Union)
realms.note: Personal union under Eric.

realms.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
realms.note: Nominally tributary to the Horde; tribute irregular after Edigu's 1408 siege.

realms.name: Golden Horde
realms.ruler: Contested: Ulugh Muhammad, Dawlat Berdi and Barak; Edigu killed 1419
realms.note: Breaking up after Edigu's fall; Bulgar (Kazan) and Astrakhan under local Tatar rulers.

realms.name: Principality of Wallachia
realms.note: Tributary since Mircea's last years; Mihail resists and falls in battle Aug 1420.

realms.name: Serbian Despotate
realms.note: Hungarian vassal holding Belgrade; also pays Ottoman tribute.

realms.name: Kingdom of Bosnia
realms.note: Magnates (Hrvoje's heirs, Sandalj Hranić) strong; Ottoman tribute.

realms.name: Zeta (Balšić)
realms.note: At war with Venice over Scutari.

realms.name: Duchy of Athens
realms.note: Pays Ottoman tribute.

realms.name: Byzantine Empire
realms.note: Constantinople, Thessaloniki (under Despot Andronikos), Black Sea towns; Ottoman peace with Mehmed I.

realms.name: Ottoman Sultanate
realms.note: Reunited since Çamurlu (1413).

realms.name: Kingdom of Cyprus
realms.note: Genoa holds Famagusta.

realms.name: Karaman
realms.ruler: Uncertain: Mehmed II captured by the Mamluks in 1419; Ali Bey installed

realms.name: Germiyan
realms.note: Restored after Ankara; left to the Ottomans by will in 1429.

realms.name: Qara Qoyunlu
realms.note: Holds Azerbaijan and Iraq (Baghdad under his son Shah Muhammad); Shah Rukh marches on him in 1420.

realms.name: Jalayirid remnant
realms.note: Rump in Khuzistan and lower Iraq after 1410-11.

realms.name: Timurid Empire
realms.note: Ulugh Beg rules Transoxiana from Samarkand; Ibrahim Sultan holds Fars.

realms.name: Rasulid Yemen
realms.note: Holds Aden.

realms.name: Delhi Sultanate (Sayyid)
realms.note: Rules as Shah Rukh's deputy in name; Punjab troubled by the Khokhars.

realms.name: Vijayanagara
realms.note: Defeats Firuz Shah at Pangal in 1420.

realms.name: Ming China
realms.note: Court already in Beijing; Beijing becomes the capital on 2 Feb 1421. Rules Jiaozhi (Dai Viet) since 1407.

realms.name: Eastern Mongols (Northern Yuan)
realms.ruler: Arughtai of the Asud; khanship contested (Oyiradai)

realms.name: Joseon
realms.ruler: Sejong (retired king Taejong holds the army)

realms.name: Chūzan (Ryukyu)
realms.ruler: Shō Hashi (with his father Shō Shishō as king)
realms.note: Destroyed Hokuzan in 1416; Nanzan (Taromai) still independent until 1429.

realms.name: Khmer Kingdom
realms.note: Still at Angkor before the Siamese sack of 1431.

realms.name: Malacca Sultanate
realms.note: Ming tributary and protected.

realms.name: Mali Empire
realms.note: Still holds Timbuktu (lost to the Tuareg in 1433).

realms.name: Sayfawa Bornu
realms.note: Sayfawa in exile west of Lake Chad.

realms.name: Adal (Walashma)
realms.note: Walashma heirs returned from Yemen c. 1415 after Ifat's fall.

realms.name: Tepanec domain
realms.note: Dominant in the Valley of Mexico; took Texcoco in 1418.

realms.name: Principality of Achaea
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Nanzan
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Judicate of Arborea
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Sold its rights to Aragon in August 1420.

realms.name: Archbishopric of Riga
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Beylik of Aydın
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Annexed by the Ottomans 1426.

realms.name: City of Cologne
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Despotate of Epirus (Tocco)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Jaffna Kingdom
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Faruqi Khandesh
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Lordship of Lucca
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Maynila
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Beylik of Menteşe
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Annexed by the Ottomans 1424.

realms.name: Marquisate of Montferrat
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Grand Principality of Ryazan
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Electorate of Saxe-Wittenberg
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Line dies out 1422; electorate passes to the Wettins.

realms.name: Republic of Siena
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sicily
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Separate kingdom in union with the Crown of Aragon since 1409, ruled by viceroys.

paris.note: Charles VI's Paris, controlled by the Burgundian party since May 1418; Henry V enters in Dec 1420.

nantes.note: Duke John V held captive by the Penthièvre Feb-Jul 1420; Breton government holds the city.

amsterdam.note: Holland governed by John of Bavaria in 1420 against Jacqueline of Hainaut's claims.

algiers.note: Hafsid since c. 1410-11 under Abu Faris; local autonomy and Zayyanid claims.

rome.note: Restored to the Church after Braccio's and Sforza's occupations of 1417; Martin V still in Florence.

palermo.note: Sicily ruled from Aragon by viceroys since 1409-12.

prague.note: Prague towns are Hussite and reject Sigismund; royal garrisons hold Hradčany and Vyšehrad. Kingdom in interregnum.

cologne.note: The city governs itself as a de facto free city; the archbishop sits in Bonn.

copenhagen.note: Crown holding since 1417 (taken from the bishop of Roskilde).

visby.note: Gotland sold by the Teutonic Order to Queen Margaret in 1408; held by the union king Eric.

riga.note: City and archbishop under the Order's lordship.

kazan.note: Bulgar-Kazan under local Tatar princes of the disintegrating Horde; the khanate forms only in 1438.

astrakhan.note: Horde lands amid civil war after Edigu's death.

sarai.note: Ruined by Timur in 1395; still a Horde seat contested between khans.

belgrade.note: Given to Stefan Lazarević by Sigismund c. 1403-04.

thessaloniki.note: Under Despot Andronikos Palaiologos; given to Venice only in 1423.

konya.note: Karaman shaken by the Mamluk campaign of 1419; ruler uncertain.

baghdad.note: Taken from the Jalayirids in 1411; governed by Shah Muhammad.

isfahan.note: Under Timurid princes (Rustam b. Umar Shaykh).

urgench.note: Khwarazm recovered from the Horde in 1413.

kashgar.note: Ulugh Beg's governors held Kashgar from c. 1416 until the Dughlats retook it; dates disputed.

lahore.note: Sayyid sovereignty; Lahore half-ruined and contested with the Khokhars of Jasrath.

gaur.note: Capital at Pandua; Gaur part of the sultanate.

ahmedabad.note: Founded by Ahmad Shah I in 1411.

colombo.note: Colombo port near the Kotte capital; Muslim merchant community.

lhasa.note: Phagmodrupa overlordship; the Gelug found Drepung (1416) and Sera (1419).

karakorum.note: Eastern Mongol (Arughtai) range, contested with the Oirat.

kamakura.note: Kanto under the Kamakura kubo, a shogunal branch.

hakata.note: Held by the shogunal Kyushu tandai (Shibukawa) against the Shoni and Otomo.

hanoi.note: Jiaozhi province since 1407; Lê Lợi's revolt since 1418 in the hills.

angkor.note: Still the royal seat; abandoned after 1431.

manila.note: Manila Bay polities (Tondo, Maynila); no single state documented for 1420.

timbuktu.note: Malian until the Tuareg take it in 1433.

gao.note: Sunni Songhai of Gao, independent of or loosely tributary to Mali.

kanem.note: Bulala hold Kanem; Sayfawa in Bornu.

mbanza_kongo.note: Kongo kingdom founded c. 1390s; early chronology uncertain.

mogadishu.note: City sultanate within the Ajuran sphere.

zeila.note: Walashma (Adal) after Ifat's destruction; Ethiopian raids; dates disputed.

tzintzuntzan.note: Lake Pátzcuaro lordships being united by Tariacuri; Tzintzuntzan a subordinate seat.

mayapan.note: Mayapan league under the Cocom; falls c. 1441-61.

havana.note: Taíno and Guanahatabey communities, no state.

quito.note: Quitu-Cara chiefdoms; degree of statehood debated.

quebec.note: St. Lawrence Iroquoian village of Stadacona, no state.

new_orleans.note: Plaquemine/Mississippian peoples, no state at the site.

singapore.note: Temasek largely abandoned after c. 1398; Orang Laut; Siamese and Malacca claims.

events.name: Zheng He's first voyage sets out
Venice takes Padua; end of the Carraresi
James of Scotland captured at sea; Robert III dies
Florence takes Pisa
Ming conquest of Dai Ngu (Ho dynasty)
Murder of Louis of Orléans
Qara Yusuf defeats and kills Miran Shah at Sardrud
Council of Pisa elects a third pope
Shah Rukh takes Samarkand and reunites the Timurid core
Battle of Grunwald (Tannenberg)
Martin of Aragon dies; Aragonese interregnum
Compromise of Caspe: Ferdinand of Antequera king of Aragon
Henry IV dies; Henry V king
Battle of Çamurlu: Mehmed I ends the Ottoman Interregnum
Khizr Khan takes Delhi; Sayyid dynasty
Council of Constance opens
Jan Hus burned at Constance
Portugal takes Ceuta
Battle of Agincourt
Venice defeats the Ottoman fleet off Gallipoli
Election of Martin V ends the Western Schism
Henry V lands in Normandy
Burgundians take Paris
Rouen surrenders to Henry V
Joseon expedition against Tsushima (Ōei invasion)
First Defenestration of Prague
Wenceslaus IV dies; Bohemian interregnum
John the Fearless murdered at Montereau
Martin V proclaims the crusade against the Hussites
Battle of Sudoměř
Treaty of Troyes

Colin Imber, The Ottoman Empire 1300-1650 (2002); Dimitris Kastritsis, The Sons of Bayezid (2007)
Beatrice Forbes Manz, Power, Politics and Religion in Timurid Iran (2007)
Frederick Heymann, John Žižka and the Hussite Revolution (1955)
The Cambridge History of China, vol. 7 (Ming, part 1)
The New Cambridge Medieval History, vol. 7 (c. 1415-c. 1500)
C. E. Bosworth, The New Islamic Dynasties (1996)
open_questions: Paris: holder given as Charles VI's France; it was governed by the Burgundian party, so a run may reasonably credit burgundy.
France is split three ways (Charles VI, the Dauphin, England); how the check maps 'france' to Charles VI's crown versus the Dauphin's realm needs a rule.
Prague: the Hussite Prague towns governed the city while Sigismund claimed the kingdom; bohemia is used with low confidence.

Golden Horde: khans in 1420 are contested (Ulugh Muhammad, Dawlat Berdi, Barak); Kazan, Astrakhan and Sarai are given to golden_horde with low confidence; id golden_horde is new (map great_horde is the 1444 rump).
Kashgar: Timurid hold c. 1416-1430s versus Dughlat rule is disputed in the sources.
Zeila and Adal: dates of Sa'ad ad-Din II's death (1410 or 1415) and of the Walashma return are disputed.
Kalmar Union shown as three realms under Eric of Pomerania; the 1444 map keeps them separate.
Great powers: hungary is included for Sigismund's imperial role; poland-lithuania (after Grunwald) has an equal case.
Karaman's ruler in May 1420 (Mamluk-installed Ali Bey or restored Mehmed II) is uncertain.
Many African, American and island rulers are unknown by name for 1420 and are marked uncertain.

Id harmonisation: realms still standing in May 1420 were added (Achaea, Nanzan, Arborea, Riga, Aydın, Menteşe, Cologne city, Tocco Epirus, Jaffna, Khandesh, Lucca, Maynila, Montferrat, Ryazan, Saxe-Wittenberg, Siena, Sicily). Sicily is carried as a separate kingdom in union with Aragon rather than ended in 1409.

Texcoco is counted as ended (conquered by the Tepanecs in 1418; refounded inside the Triple Alliance). Khizr Khan's Multan (1405) is counted as ended when he took Delhi (1414); the 1444 multan is the later Langah/Qureshi state under the same map id.
